sys_atf_test.name: Day-2 happy path: password reset closes with evidence
sys_atf_test.description: Order the password-reset catalog item as a requester with a distinct approver; approve it; assert the client actuated, the gate verified, the target reconciled, and the request closed carrying the evidence record.

sys_atf_step.description: Assert the preconditions this test depends on: test_mode is on (no live Graph) and a MID server is configured. Fail fast and loudly rather than silently exercising a real tenant.

sys_atf_step.step_config_title: Service Catalog - Order the "Day-2 identity request" item (password reset)
sys_atf_step.description: Impersonate day2.requester. Set control_key = entra.credential.password_reset, target_user = a reconciled test identity, requester_id = day2.requester, approver_id = day2.servicedesk (DISTINCT), justification populated. Order Now; capture the RITM. Note the form never collects a temporary password — it is MID-generated (IA-5).
Assert the gate's pre-flight passed for a well-formed request (distinct requester/approver, non-privileged).
Impersonate day2.servicedesk (the approver, NOT the requester) and approve. This is the L3 human-approval step — the loop must not have actuated before it.
sys_atf_step.inputs: approve the sysapproval_approver record assigned to day2.servicedesk

sys_atf_step.description: Assert the client actuated the reset (test_mode canned response) and the gate's post-actuation verify confirmed it. Actuation is Graph-via-MID; ServiceNow never wrote to the estate.
Assert the request closed complete AND carries the evidence record (the artifact an assessor reads). A closed request with no evidence is a silent control failure.
